title: Synthesis of a Large Functional Cage Compound Based on Four GaGa Single Bonds and Its Application as an Oligoacceptor: On the Way to Bio‐Organogallium Hybrid Molecules
abstract: AbstractThe digallium compound R2GaGaR2 (1; R=CH(SiMe3)2) reacts with citracinic acid by the release of two equivalents of bis(trimethylsilyl)methane and the formation of a unique oligofunctional cage compound (2). Four GaGa bonds in a tetrahedral arrangement are bridged by four spacer ligands that are located on the faces of the tetrahedron and bridge the gallium atoms of three different GaGa bonds. Four pyridinium groups result from the shift of one of the three acidic protons of four citracinic acid molecules to the nitrogen atoms of the aromatic rings. The NH groups are arranged in pairs and are capable of acting as chelating acceptors for the coordination of THF molecules (2(THF)2) or the nitrogen atoms of 1‐deazapurine (3(OEt2)4). In particular, the last reaction verifies the potential applicability of this relatively water‐ and air‐resistant acceptor compound for the generation of bioorganometallic hybrid molecules.
